description: A recreation of the 1972 Triadex Muse: eight sliders tap a set of binary counters and a thirty-one bit shift register, and their interaction makes a long melody nobody wrote

params.text: Picks which of the forty taps this slider reads for the theme; the four theme taps are combined and the result is fed back into the shift register, which is what shapes the pattern over the long run
Picks which of the forty taps this slider reads for the interval; the four interval taps form a four-bit number each clock, three bits choosing a note and the fourth adding an octave
Starts and stops the sequence on each press; the lamp is lit while it runs
Clears the counters and the shift register and starts the pattern again on each press
Draws fresh positions for the sliders on each press, over whichever sliders the menu has it set to touch
Picks the scale the interval bits read, from the same list the other modules use

inputs.text: Each rise advances the engine by one step; the module has no tempo of its own
A rise clears the counters and the shift register and starts the pattern again
A high gate runs the sequence, taking the run button's place
A rise draws fresh positions for the sliders
Moves that interval slider's tap choice, ±5V added to the slider
Moves that theme slider's tap choice, ±5V added to the slider
Transposes the melody, a volt per octave added to the root knob
Picks the scale, added to the scale knob; it takes the same signal another module's scale output sends

outputs.text: The melody as a volt per octave, with the scale and the root applied, or rescaled to a fixed span when the menu sets an output range
A trigger on each step, or only on the steps where the pitch changes, depending on the menu

notes: the module has no clock of its own: nothing moves until a clock is patched and the sequence is running
a slider can point at OFF, ON, the raw clock, six counter bits or the thirty-one shift-register bits, and the lamp column beside the sliders shows each tap moment by moment
menu: Presets (from Triadex manual) — a submenu of seventeen slider settings taken from the original 1972 manual, each loading all eight sliders at once
Output range — a label over the four choices below it
V/oct — sends the melody out as a standard volt per octave with the root applied
1V — rescales the melody's whole span into one volt and ignores the root, for use as modulation rather than pitch
2V — rescales the melody's whole span into two volts and ignores the root
5V — rescales the melody's whole span into five volts and ignores the root
Link — a label over the linking choice below it
Allow expander linking (adjacent Muse → follow) — makes a second Muse placed immediately to the right follow this one's engine, so several can be chained off one pattern
Gate — a label over the two choices below it
Every clock pulse — fires the gate output on every step
Only when pitch changes — fires the gate output only where the melody moves, so repeated notes are tied together
Randomize — a label over the four items below it
All 8 sliders — makes the randomize button and jack draw fresh positions for every slider
Theme only — makes the randomize button and jack touch the four theme sliders alone
Interval only — makes the randomize button and jack touch the four interval sliders alone
Randomize now — draws fresh slider positions at once, over whichever sliders the scope above allows
